page: Vultr vc2-16c-64gb is an x86_64 cloud server instance within the Cloud Compute family, configured with 16 shared vCPUs mapped across 8 physical Intel Xeon cores running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache, with support for AVX, AVX-512F, and AES instruction sets. System memory totals 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. High-speed local persistence is supplied via a bundled 1280 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without dedicated GPU acceleration hardware.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a distinction between single-threaded and parallel processing capabilities. In single-core tests, the 2.0 GHz clock speed results in modest throughput, characterized by a Geekbench single-core score of 836.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 23.39 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics scale across the 16 virtual cores, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 21511.0, a multi-core Geekbench score of 6565.0, and a stress-ng multi-core rating of 21535.52. Memory subsystem testing demonstrates read bandwidth of 107.12 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 53.71 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB blocks, supporting Redis throughput of 23.04 million SET operations per second and web serving delivery at 12.01 GB/sec.

The shared vCPU model and lower clock frequency present performance trade-offs for latency-sensitive, single-threaded execution, but deliver solid qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded and resource-dense applications. Bundling 64.0 GB of RAM and 1280 GB of fast NVMe storage makes this configuration well aligned for memory-backed caching, intermediate database hosting, batch data processing, build automation, and general containerized web applications.

Benchmark evaluations show balanced multi-threaded performance, recording 21511.0 on PassMark CPU, 6565.0 on Geekbench multi-core, and 23.04 million Redis SET operations per second, though single-core metrics reflect lower throughput due to the shared 2.0 GHz clock. With a balanced memory-to-core ratio and significant local storage capacity, the instance offers strong qualitative resource value for multi-threaded workloads such as database management, distributed caching, containerized web clusters, and continuous integration pipelines.
